### Step 0: Install and load required packages

```{r}
#| eval: false
# we recommend running this is a fresh R session or restarting your current session
install.packages(
    "cmdstanr",
    repos = c('https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev', getOption("repos"))
)
library(cmdstanr)
# Check toolchains
check_cmdstan_toolchain()
# If toolcahin is not setup properly, follow the printed instructions, or visit https://mc-stan.org/docs/cmdstan-guide/installation.html#cpp-toolchain
# Install cmdstan
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()
# We also install the bayesplot package visualizing MCMC results
install.packages("bayesplot")
```

```{r}
library(cmdstanr)
register_knitr_engine()
options(mc.cores = min(parallel::detectCores() - 1, 4)) # Use four CPU cores for MCMC sampling, if available
library(bayesplot)
library(HDInterval)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
# Define function for HDI
hdi2 <- function(x, cred_mass = 0.90) {
    hdi_interval <- HDInterval::hdi(x, credMass = cred_mass)
    setNames(hdi_interval, c("hdi_lo", "hdi_hi"))
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::knit_engines$set(stan = function(options) {
    output_var <- options$output.var
    if (options$eval) {
        dir <- if (options$cache) {
            paste0(options$cache.path %||% "", options$label)
        } else {
            tempdir()
        }
        file <- cmdstanr::write_stan_file(options$code, dir = dir)
        engine_opts <- options$engine.opts %||% list()
        mod <- do.call(
            cmdstanr::cmdstan_model,
            c(list(stan_file = file), engine_opts)
        )
        assign(output_var, mod, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    }
    options$engine <- "stan"
    knitr::engine_output(options, paste(options$code, collapse = "\n"), "")
})
```

### Step 1: Data import

```{r}
set.seed(1234)
n_mz <- c(325, 60, 7, 78, 150, 40, 8, 38, 88)
n_dz <- c(202, 97, 19, 96, 112, 64, 46, 56, 66)
# Convert to long format data frame
dat_mz <- data.frame(
    twin1 = rep(rep(1:3, 3), n_mz),
    twin2 = rep(rep(1:3, each = 3), n_mz)
)
dat_dz <- data.frame(
    twin1 = rep(rep(1:3, 3), n_dz),
    twin2 = rep(rep(1:3, each = 3), n_dz)
)
dat_mz[] <- lapply(dat_mz, ordered, labels = c("normal", "overweight", "obese"))
dat_dz[] <- lapply(dat_dz, ordered, labels = c("normal", "overweight", "obese"))
dat_full <- rbind(
    data.frame(zygosity = "MZ", dat_mz),
    data.frame(zygosity = "DZ", dat_dz)
)
sub_n <- 100
dat <- dat_full[sample.int(nrow(dat_full), 100), ]
# dat <- dat_full
```

```{r}
str(dat)
summary(dat)
```

```{r}
tab_mz <- with(dat[dat$zygosity == "MZ", ], table(twin1, twin2))
tab_dz <- with(dat[dat$zygosity == "DZ", ], table(twin1, twin2))
```

### Step 2: Compile the Stan model

```{stan}
#| eval: !expr '!file.exists(here::here("notebooks", "ace_fit.rds"))'
#| output.var: "ace"
#| file: !expr here::here("stan", "ace_ordinal_symmetry.stan")
#| engine.opts: !expr list(include_paths = here::here("stan"))
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: false
ace <- cmdstan_model(here::here("stan", "ace_ordinal_symmetry.stan"))
```

### Step 3: Prepare data and sampling

```{r}
# Reduced frequency vector
to_ltri <- function(tab_x) {
    symm_x <- tab_x + t(tab_x) - diag(diag(tab_x))
    ltri_x <- symm_x[lower.tri(symm_x, diag = TRUE)]
}
(ltri_nmz <- to_ltri(tab_mz))
(ltri_ndz <- to_ltri(tab_dz))
```

```{r}
#| eval: !expr '!file.exists(here::here("notebooks", "ace_fit.rds"))'
ace_fit <- ace$sample(
    list(k = 3, ltri_ns1 = ltri_nmz, ltri_ns2 = ltri_ndz),
    chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000,
    iter_sampling = 1000,
    seed = 732 # for reproducibility
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
if (!file.exists(here::here("notebooks", "ace_fit.rds"))) {
    ace_fit$save_object(here::here("notebooks", "ace_fit.rds"))
} else {
    ace_fit <- readRDS(here::here("notebooks", "ace_fit.rds"))
}
```

### Step 4: Check convergence

```{r}
params <- c("rho1", "rho2", "thres", "h2", "c2", "e2")
ace_fit$print(params)
ace_fit$diagnostic_summary()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-rank-hist
#| fig-cap: Rank histograms for the main model parameters
ace_fit$draws(params) |>
    mcmc_rank_hist()
```

### Step 5: Model checking

#### Repeat Steps 3 and 4 with reparameterized model

With unreasonable h2 and c2, we reparameterize the model to enforce theory-informed priors/constraints.

```{stan}
#| eval: !expr '!file.exists(here::here("notebooks", "ace_s_fit.rds"))'
#| output.var: "ace_simplex"
#| file: !expr here::here("stan", "ace_ordinal_symmetry_simplex.stan")
#| engine.opts: !expr list(include_paths = here::here("stan"))
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: false
ace_simplex <- cmdstan_model(here::here(
    "stan",
    "ace_ordinal_symmetry_simplex.stan"
))
```

One can then repeat steps 3 and 4 to obtain the posterior samples and convergence diagnostics, which we do not repeat the details here. The posterior summaries of the main parameters are in @tbl-post-summ.

```{r}
#| eval: !expr '!file.exists(here::here("notebooks", "ace_s_fit.rds"))'
ace_s_fit <- ace_simplex$sample(
    list(k = 3, ltri_ns1 = ltri_nmz, ltri_ns2 = ltri_ndz),
    chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000,
    iter_sampling = 1000,
    seed = 732 # for reproducibility
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
if (!file.exists(here::here("notebooks", "ace_s_fit.rds"))) {
    ace_s_fit$save_object(here::here("notebooks", "ace_s_fit.rds"))
} else {
    ace_s_fit <- readRDS(here::here("notebooks", "ace_s_fit.rds"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-post-summ
#| tbl-cap: Posterior summary of the main model parameters, based on the simplex parameterization
ace_s_fit$summary(params, mean, median, sd, mad, posterior::quantile2, hdi2) |>
    transform(
        variable = paste0(
            variable,
            " (",
            c(
                "$\\rho^\\text{MZ}$",
                "$\\rho^\\text{DZ}$",
                "$\\tau_1$",
                "$\\tau_2$",
                "$h^2$",
                "$c^2$",
                "$e^2$"
            ),
            ")"
        )
    ) |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

#### Global fit

```{r}
#| include: false
ace_s_fit$summary(c("X2_1_samp", "X2_1_gt", "X2_2_samp", "X2_2_gt"))
```

#### Local fit

```{r}
x_scale <- scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(ltri_nmz),
    labels = c(
        "(1,1)",
        "(2,1)+(1,2)",
        "(2,2)",
        "(3,1)+(1,3)",
        "(3,2)+(2,3)",
        "(3,3)"
    )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-intervals-mz
#| fig-cap: Posterior predictive check for each cell count in the contingency tables for MZ twins
ace_s_fit$draws("ltri_ns1_tilde", format = "matrix") |>
    ppc_intervals(y = ltri_nmz) +
    xlab("Cell (twin1, twin2)") +
    x_scale
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-intervals-dz
#| fig-cap: Posterior predictive check for each cell count in the contingency tables for DZ twins
ace_s_fit$draws("ltri_ns2_tilde", format = "matrix") |>
    ppc_intervals(y = ltri_ndz) +
    xlab("Cell (twin1, twin2)") +
    x_scale
```

### Step 6: Summarizing the posterior

```{r}
#| label: fig-post-dens
#| fig-cap: Posterior distributions of the main model parameters
ace_s_fit$draws(params) |>
    mcmc_hist()
```

### Compare with *umx* package

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| error: true
library(umx)
# Make the ordinal variables into umxFactors
dat[, c("twin1", "twin2")] <- umxFactor(dat[, c("twin1", "twin2")])

mz_data <- dat[dat$zygosity == "MZ", ]
dz_data <- dat[dat$zygosity == "DZ", ]

# Model and summary with FIML
m1 <- umxACE(
    selDVs = "twin",
    dzData = dz_data,
    mzData = mz_data,
    sep = "",
    tryHard = "ordinal"
)
umxSummary(m1)
```

```{r}
# CI failed
umxConfint(m1, run = TRUE)
```


```{r}
# Model and summary with DWLS
m1_dwls <- umxACE(
    selDVs = "twin",
    dzData = dz_data,
    mzData = mz_data,
    sep = "",
    type = "DWLS",
    tryHard = "ordinal"
)
umxSummary(m1_dwls)
```

```{r}
# Extremely large standard errors
summary(m1_dwls)
```

```{r}
# Model and summary with WLS
m1_wls <- umxACE(
    selDVs = "twin",
    dzData = dz_data,
    mzData = mz_data,
    sep = "",
    type = "WLS",
    tryHard = "ordinal"
)
umxSummary(m1_wls)
```

```{r}
# CI failed
umxConfint(m1_wls, run = TRUE)
```
